title: Act Three. Bhava-prakasha (The Revealing of Feeling)
html:
Radha despairs at Krishna's feigned refusal; her friends console her; Madhavi brings from Krishna a picture with Radha's portrait and a verse, a sign of His love; Radha sends Madanika to Krishna.

(Enter Ashoka-manjari.)

Ashoka-manjari (Prakrit). Ah, I have heard that my dear friend, with Madanika, the Forest-goddess and Shashimukhi, is sitting near the bower of madhavi creepers, plotting some secret. I'll take a look and go. (Looking ahead and approaching.) Ah, they are whispering something very softly. It would not be right for me to go in there. (Exit.)

(Enter Radha, being admonished by Shashimukhi and Madanika.)

Radha (sighing long and hot, Prakrit). So Madhava has really rejected me!

Song 9 — in raga Sama-gurjari.

Song 9 (3)

कुलवनिताजनधृतमाचारं
तृणवदगणयं गलितविचारम् ॥
शिव शिव किं वा चरितमशस्तं
विधिरधुना वद वशयतु कस्तम् ॥ ध्रु ॥
शिशुरपि युवतिरिवाहितभावा
विगलितलज्जितमहमिव का वा ॥
गजपतिरुद्रमुदे समुदीतं
रामानन्दरायकविगीतम् ॥ ३ ॥

kulavanitājanadhṛtamācāraṁ
tṛṇavadagaṇayaṁ galitavicāram ||
śiva śiva kiṁ vā caritamaśastaṁ
vidhiradhunā vada vaśayatu kastam || dhru ||
śiśurapi yuvatirivāhitabhāvā
vigalitalajjitamahamiva kā vā ||
gajapatirudramude samudītaṁ
rāmānandarāyakavigītam || 3 ||

kula-vanitā-jana-dhṛtam — kept by women of good family; ācāram — the conduct; tṛṇavat — as a straw; agaṇayam — I counted; galita-vicāram — having lost my reason; śiva śiva — O Shiva, Shiva; kiṁ vā — what; caritam — deed; aśastam — unworthy; vidhiḥ — Fate; adhunā — now; vada — say; vaśayatu — will win over; kaḥ — who; tam — Him; śiśuḥ api — though a child; yuvatiḥ iva — like a young woman; āhita-bhāvā — filled with feelings; vigalita-lajjitam — who has cast off shame; aham iva — like me; kā vā — who else; gajapati-rudra-mude — for the joy of Gajapati Rudra; samuditam — has been sung; rāmānanda-rāya-kavi-gītam — the song of the poet Ramananda Raya.

3The conduct that women of good family keep, I, losing my reason, counted as a straw. O Shiva, Shiva, what an unworthy thing I have done! Say, Fate: who now will win Him over? (Refrain.) I am still a girl, yet I am full of feelings like a grown woman; who else, like me, has thrown off shame? For the joy of Gajapati Rudra this song of the poet Ramananda Raya has been sung.1

Shashimukhi (Prakrit). I have told you everything as it happened; so judge for yourself.

Radha (using Sanskrit).

Verse 5

श्रावं श्रावं सुसामश्रुतिसमितपरब्रह्म वंशीप्रसूतं
दर्शं दर्शं त्रिलोकीवरतरुणकलाकेलिलावण्यसारम् ।
ध्यायं ध्यायं समुद्यद्द्युमणिकुमुदिनीबन्धुरोचिः सरोचि-
श्चायं(?) श्रीकान्तसंगं(?) दहति मम मनो मां कुकूलाग्निदाहम् ॥ ५ ॥

śrāvaṁ śrāvaṁ susāmaśrutisamitaparabrahma vaṁśīprasūtaṁ
darśaṁ darśaṁ trilokīvarataruṇakalākelilāvaṇyasāram |
dhyāyaṁ dhyāyaṁ samudyaddyumaṇikumudinībandhurociḥ saroci-
ścāyaṁ(?) śrīkāntasaṁgaṁ(?) dahati mama mano māṁ kukūlāgnidāham || 5 ||

śrāvaṁ śrāvam — hearing again and again; su-sāma-śruti-samita — in harmony with the fair Sama chants; para-brahma — the Parabrahman; vaṁśī-prasūtam — born of the flute; darśaṁ darśam — seeing again and again; tri-lokī-vara-taruṇa — of the finest youth of the three worlds; kalā-keli — skilled in play; lāvaṇya-sāram — the essence of beauty; dhyāyaṁ dhyāyam — meditating again and again; samudyad-dyumaṇi — of the rising sun; kumudinī-bandhu — and the moon (friend of lilies); rociḥ — lustre; śrī-kānta — beloved of Shri; dahati — burns; mama — my; manaḥ — mind; mām — me; kukūla-agni-dāham — as a fire of chaff burns.

5Hearing again and again the sound of His flute, the Parabrahman in harmony with the fair chants of the Sama Veda; seeing again and again the essence of the beauty of the finest youth of the three worlds, skilled in play; meditating again and again on Him, radiant as the rising sun and the moon — the beloved of Shri — I feel my mind burning me like a smouldering fire of chaff.2

Shashimukhi (using Sanskrit). Friend, give up this misplaced insistence.

Verse 7

यद्यद्व्यञ्जितमञ्जनप्रतिकृतौ(?) कृष्णे तदर्थं मया
तत्तत्तेन निवारितं शिशुदशाभावप्रकाशैरलम् ।
आस्तामुत्कलिकाप्रसूनविगलन्माध्वीकनद्धं विषं
कृष्णध्यानमितोऽन्यतः सुवदने संकल्पमाकल्पय ॥ ७ ॥

yadyadvyañjitamañjanapratikṛtau(?) kṛṣṇe tadarthaṁ mayā
tattattena nivāritaṁ śiśudaśābhāvaprakāśairalam |
āstāmutkalikāprasūnavigalanmādhvīkanaddhaṁ viṣaṁ
kṛṣṇadhyānamito'nyataḥ suvadane saṁkalpamākalpaya || 7 ||

yad yad — whatever; vyañjitam — was expressed; kṛṣṇe — to Krishna; tad-artham — for your sake; mayā — by me; tat tat — all that; tena — by Him; nivāritam — warded off; śiśu-daśā-bhāva-prakāśaiḥ — by showing the state of a child; alam — enough; āstām — let it be; utkalikā-prasūna — from the flowers of longing; vigalan-mādhvīka — with dripping honey; naddham — steeped; viṣam — poison; kṛṣṇa-dhyānam — the thought of Krishna; itaḥ anyataḥ — elsewhere; suvadane — fair-faced one; saṅkalpam — desire; ākalpaya — turn.

7Whatever I told Krishna for your sake, He warded it all off by making a show of being a mere child. Enough! Let that poison be — the thought of Krishna, steeped in the honey dripping from the flowers of your longing; turn your desire elsewhere, fair-faced one.3

Song 10 — in raga Suhayi.

Song 10 (8)

हीनं पतिमपि भजते रमणी
केशरिणं किमु कलयति हरिणी ॥
राधिके परिहर माधवरागम् ॥ ध्रु ॥
क्षीणे शशिनि च कुमुदवनीयं
भजति न भावं किमु रमणीयम् ॥
सुखयतु गजपतिरुद्रनरेशं
रामानन्दरायगीतमनिशम् ॥ ८ ॥

hīnaṁ patimapi bhajate ramaṇī
keśariṇaṁ kimu kalayati hariṇī ||
rādhike parihara mādhavarāgam || dhru ||
kṣīṇe śaśini ca kumudavanīyaṁ
bhajati na bhāvaṁ kimu ramaṇīyam ||
sukhayatu gajapatirudranareśaṁ
rāmānandarāyagītamaniśam || 8 ||

hīnam — unworthy; patim — husband; api — even; bhajate — serves; ramaṇī — a woman; keśariṇam — a lion; kimu — does; kalayati — choose; hariṇī — a doe; rādhike — O Radhika; parihara — give up; mādhava-rāgam — love for Madhava; kṣīṇe — waning; śaśini — for the moon; ca — and; kumuda-vanī iyam — this forest of lilies; bhajati na — does it not bear; bhāvam — feeling; kimu — whether; ramaṇīyam — lovely; sukhayatu — may it delight; gajapati-rudra-nareśam — King Gajapati Rudra; rāmānanda-rāya-gītam — the song of Ramananda Raya; aniśam — ever.

8A woman serves her husband even if he is unworthy; does a doe choose a lion?
Radhika, give up your love for Madhava! (Refrain.)
And when the moon wanes, does the forest of night-lilies cease to love it?4
May Ramananda Raya's song ever delight King Gajapati Rudra.

Radha (in tears). Lady Madanika, what is this?

Verse 9

प्रेमच्छेदरुजोऽवगच्छति हरिर्नायं न च प्रेम वा
स्थानास्थानमवैति नापि मदनो जानाति नो दुर्बलाः ।
अन्यो वेद न चान्यदुःखमखिलं नो जीवनं वाश्रवं(?)
द्वित्राण्येव दिनानि यौवनमिदं हाहा विधेः का गतिः ॥ ९ ॥

premacchedarujo'vagacchati harirnāyaṁ na ca prema vā
sthānāsthānamavaiti nāpi madano jānāti no durbalāḥ |
anyo veda na cānyaduḥkhamakhilaṁ no jīvanaṁ vāśravaṁ(?)
dvitrāṇyeva dināni yauvanamidaṁ hāhā vidheḥ kā gatiḥ || 9 ||

prema-ccheda-rujaḥ — the pains of love broken off; avagacchati na — does not know; hariḥ ayam — this Hari; na ca — nor; prema — love; vā — indeed; sthāna-asthānam — what is fit and unfit; avaiti — discerns; na api — nor; madanaḥ — Madana; jānāti — knows; naḥ — us; durbalāḥ — weak; anyaḥ — another; veda na — does not know; ca — and; anya-duḥkham — another's grief; akhilam — wholly; naḥ — our; jīvanam — life; āśravam(?) — not in our power; dvitrāṇi eva — only two or three; dināni — days; yauvanam idam — this youth; hāhā — alas; vidheḥ — of Fate; kā — what; gatiḥ — course.

9Hari does not know the pain of love broken off; love does not know what is its place and what is not; Madana does not understand that we are weak; no one knows another's pain in full; our life is not in our power; and this youth lasts but two or three days. Alas, alas, what a course Fate takes!5

Madanika. Why do you torment yourself so? For:

Verse 10

समाकृष्टा दूरात्किमपि यदि सा केतकिवनप्रसूने(?) …
… सुरभिभरसारेण नियतम् ।
अथ भ्रामं भ्रामं रजसि रसमालोक्य न मनाग्
अपि प्रान्तं प्राप्ता परिहरति तं नो मधुकरी ॥ १० ॥

samākṛṣṭā dūrātkimapi yadi sā ketakivanaprasūne(?) …
… surabhibharasāreṇa niyatam |
atha bhrāmaṁ bhrāmaṁ rajasi rasamālokya na manāg
api prāntaṁ prāptā pariharati taṁ no madhukarī || 10 ||

samākṛṣṭā — drawn; dūrāt — from afar; yadi — if; ketaki-vana-prasūne — to the ketaki flower; surabhi-bhara-sāreṇa — by the strength of rich fragrance; niyatam — surely; atha — then; bhrāmaṁ bhrāmam — circling and circling; rajasi — in the pollen; rasam — nectar; ālokya na manāk — finding little; api — even; prāntaṁ prāptā — having reached; pariharati — abandons; tam — it; no — not; madhukarī — the bee.

10If a bee, drawn from afar by the rich fragrance of a ketaki flower, has come to it — then even if, circling and circling, she finds little nectar in its pollen, once she has reached it she does not leave it.6

Radha (taking courage). "He has rejected me already" — having said this only half-way, in fear and trembling: Lady, this is not my fault. For

Verse 11

यदा यातो दैवान्मधुरिपुरसौ लोचनपथं
तदास्माकं चेतो मदनहतकेनाहृतमभूत् ।
पुनर्यस्मिन्नेष क्षणमपि दृशोरेति पदवीं
विधास्यामस्तस्मिन्निखिलघटिका रत्नखचिताः ॥ ११ ॥

yadā yāto daivānmadhuripurasau locanapathaṁ
tadāsmākaṁ ceto madanahatakenāhṛtamabhūt |
punaryasminneṣa kṣaṇamapi dṛśoreti padavīṁ
vidhāsyāmastasminnikhilaghaṭikā ratnakhacitāḥ || 11 ||

yadā — when; yātaḥ — came; daivāt — by fate; madhu-ripuḥ asau — this Enemy of Madhu; locana-patham — into the path of the eyes; tadā — then; asmākam — our; cetaḥ — heart; madana-hatakena — by the wretch Madana; āhṛtam abhūt — was stolen; punaḥ — again; yasmin — when; eṣaḥ — He; kṣaṇam api — even for a moment; dṛśoḥ eti padavīm — enters the path of the eyes; vidhāsyāmaḥ — we shall make; tasmin — then; akhila-ghaṭikāḥ — all the moments; ratna-khacitāḥ — studded with jewels.

11when by the will of fate the Enemy of Madhu came into the path of my eyes, then that wretch Madana stole my heart. (Pausing a moment and sighing long and hot.) If He comes again even for a moment into the path of my eyes, I shall set every moment of that time with jewels.7

Madanika (aside). Her love has passed all bounds. Let me divert her mind with the most welcome news. (Aloud.) Child, look, look:

Verse 13

योऽयं त्वया स्वकरपुष्करसिक्तमूलं
संवर्धितः सुतनु बालरसालशाखी ।
जातः स ते मुकुलदन्तुरमौलिरीष-
न्मन्ये तदेव मधुपाः प्रियमालपन्ति ॥ १३ ॥

yo'yaṁ tvayā svakarapuṣkarasiktamūlaṁ
saṁvardhitaḥ sutanu bālarasālaśākhī |
jātaḥ sa te mukuladanturamaulirīṣa-
nmanye tadeva madhupāḥ priyamālapanti || 13 ||

yaḥ ayam — that which; tvayā — by you; sva-kara-puṣkara-sikta-mūlam — its roots watered from the lotus of your hand; saṁvardhitaḥ — was raised; sutanu — lovely one; bāla-rasāla-śākhī — young mango tree; jātaḥ — has become; saḥ — it; te — your; mukula-dantura-mauliḥ — with crown bristling with buds; īṣat — slightly; manye — I think; tad eva — therefore; madhupāḥ — the bees; priyam ālapanti — speak sweet words.

13The young mango tree that you, lovely one, raised by watering its roots from the lotus of your hand — its crown is now bristling with buds; I think that is why the bees are speaking sweet words to it.8

Radha (in fear and trembling). Friend Shashimukhi, remember me!9

Madanika (aside). Ah, what a train of misfortunes has come upon us! (Aloud.) Child, do not lose heart so: I have noticed that His heart is full of love.

Song 11 — in raga Deshaga.

Song 11 (15)

सरसकथासु कथं पुलकाचितमाननकमलमजस्रं
कलयत चारु हसितनववलितं परिहृतकेलिसहस्रम् ॥
मुग्धे परिहर शङ्कितमधिकमये ॥ ध्रु ॥
आदरमधुरमिमामनुवेलं कथमालपति ससारं
सुमुखि सखीं तव तदपि मनो बत कलयति किमु न विचारम् ॥
गजपतिरुद्रनराधिपहृदये वसतु चिरं रससारे
रामानन्दरायकविभणितं परिचितकेलिविचारे ॥ १५ ॥

sarasakathāsu kathaṁ pulakācitamānanakamalamajasraṁ
kalayata cāru hasitanavavalitaṁ parihṛtakelisahasram ||
mugdhe parihara śaṅkitamadhikamaye || dhru ||
ādaramadhuramimāmanuvelaṁ kathamālapati sasāraṁ
sumukhi sakhīṁ tava tadapi mano bata kalayati kimu na vicāram ||
gajapatirudranarādhipahṛdaye vasatu ciraṁ rasasāre
rāmānandarāyakavibhaṇitaṁ paricitakelivicāre || 15 ||

sarasa-kathāsu — at sweet tales; katham — how; pulaka-ācitam — covered with gooseflesh; ānana-kamalam — the lotus face; ajasram — constantly; kalayata — behold; cāru — charmingly; hasita-nava-valitam — lit with a fresh smile; parihṛta-keli-sahasram — leaving thousands of games; mugdhe — innocent one; parihara — give up; śaṅkitam — fear; adhikam — excessive; ādara-madhuram — with respect and tenderness; imām — her; anuvelam — again and again; katham — how; ālapati — speaks; sa-sāram — about the essential; sumukhi — fair-faced one; sakhīṁ tava — to your friend; tad api — yet; manaḥ — mind; bata — ah; kalayati na — does not consider; vicāram — this; gajapati-rudra-narādhipa-hṛdaye — in the heart of Gajapati Rudra, lord of men; vasatu — may it dwell; ciram — long; rasa-sāre — the essence of rasa; rāmānanda-rāya-kavi-bhaṇitam — spoken by the poet Ramananda Raya; paricita-keli-vicāre — versed in the knowledge of play.

15Look: how is it that His lotus face constantly bristles with gooseflesh at sweet tales? How does He, leaving thousands of games, smile so charmingly with a fresh smile? Innocent one, give up your excessive fears! (Refrain.) How He speaks again and again, with respect and tenderness, to your friend about the heart of the matter, fair-faced one! Can your mind not reason about this?10 May these words of the poet Ramananda Raya long dwell in the heart of Gajapati Rudra, lord of men, which is the very essence of rasa and versed in the knowledge of play.

Radha. Lady,

Verse 16

अनुमितमम्बु पयोदे तनुपरिकलिता दावानलज्वाला ।
वपुरतिललितं बाला शिव शिव भविता कथं हरिणी ॥ १६ ॥

anumitamambu payode tanuparikalitā dāvānalajvālā |
vapuratilalitaṁ bālā śiva śiva bhavitā kathaṁ hariṇī || 16 ||

anumitam — is inferred; ambu — water; payode — in the cloud; tanu-parikalitā — has seized the body; dāvānala-jvālā — the flame of the forest fire; vapuḥ — body; ati-lalitam — very tender; bālā — a child; śiva śiva — O Shiva, Shiva; bhavitā — will survive; katham — how; hariṇī — the doe.

16water is only guessed at in the cloud, while the flames of the forest fire have already seized the body. The body is so tender and she is still a child — O Shiva, Shiva, how will the doe survive?11

Madanika. Child, to find this out I sent Madhavi with a picture bearing your likeness.

(Enter Madhavi with a picture in her hand.)

Madhavi. Lady, I bow to you.

Madanika. Welcome, child. Have you too learnt the secret?

Madhavi. Of course.

Madanika. Then tell it.

Madhavi (shows the picture).

Radha (bashfully asks for the picture).

Madhavi. First give me a reward for good news!

Madanika (aside). Surely Mukunda, clearly understanding her heart, has fallen in love too.

Unnumbered half-verse (3.25a)

भग्नः कदाचिद्यदयं प्रमादा-
त्प्रेमाङ्कुरो योजयितुं न शक्यः ॥

bhagnaḥ kadācidyadayaṁ pramādā-
tpremāṅkuro yojayituṁ na śakyaḥ ||

bhagnaḥ — broken; kadācit — ever; yat — since; ayam — this; pramādāt — through carelessness; prema-aṅkuraḥ — sprout of love; yojayitum — to join; na śakyaḥ — cannot be.

(Unnumbered.) "For if the sprout of love should ever break through carelessness, it cannot be joined again."

(Aloud.) Child, hand over the picture.

Madhavi (showing it a little, covers it with the edge of her garment).

Shashimukhi (seizing it by force, looks at it. Prakrit). Ah, what are these letters? (Reads.)

Verse 27

मा शङ्किष्ठाः सुमुखि विमुखीभावमेतस्य न स्या-
दानन्दाय प्रथममुकुला पद्मिनी कस्य कामम् ।
आघ्रायैव प्रशिथिलधृतिर्गन्धमस्यास्तथापि
नालं वेत्तुं(?) क्षणमपि युवा किं नु मध्यस्थभावम् ॥ २७ ॥

mā śaṅkiṣṭhāḥ sumukhi vimukhībhāvametasya na syā-
dānandāya prathamamukulā padminī kasya kāmam |
āghrāyaiva praśithiladhṛtirgandhamasyāstathāpi
nālaṁ vettuṁ(?) kṣaṇamapi yuvā kiṁ nu madhyasthabhāvam || 27 ||

mā śaṅkiṣṭhāḥ — do not fear; sumukhi — fair-faced one; vimukhī-bhāvam — turning away; etasya — his; na syāt — would not be; ānandāya — for the delight; prathama-mukulā — first-opening; padminī — lotus; kasya — of whom; kāmam — truly; āghrāya eva — just on smelling; praśithila-dhṛtiḥ — losing composure; gandham asyāḥ — her fragrance; tathāpi — still; na alam — is not able; vettum(?) — to adopt; kṣaṇam api — even for a moment; yuvā — the youth; kiṁ nu — how; madhyastha-bhāvam — indifference.

27"Do not fear, fair-faced one, that he has turned away from you: whom would a lotus opening for the first time not delight? And though the youth loses his composure at the very first breath of its fragrance — how could he remain indifferent even for a moment?"12

Madhavi (Prakrit). Friend, may you flourish in your beloved's love!

Radha (sighing long and hot, Prakrit). Ah, friend, where would we find such good fortune? (To Madanika.) What does this mean?

Madanika. This: clearly understanding your heart, Mukunda too has fallen in love. "For if the sprout of love should ever break through carelessness, it cannot be joined again." So, child, do not be distressed: the tree of our desires has borne fruit.

Radha (Prakrit). Even now I do not believe it. You alone are my refuge here.

Madanika. Here I go then; give me leave.

Radha (bowing, using Sanskrit). Revered lady,

Verse 33

निकुञ्जोऽयं गुञ्जन्मधुकरकदम्बाकुलतरः
प्रयातः प्रायोऽयं चरमगिरिशृङ्गं दिनमणिः ।
मरुन्मन्दं मन्दं तरलयति मल्लीमधुकरान्
किमन्यद्वक्तव्यं विधुरपि विधाता समुदयम् ॥ ३३ ॥

nikuñjo'yaṁ guñjanmadhukarakadambākulataraḥ
prayātaḥ prāyo'yaṁ caramagiriśṛṅgaṁ dinamaṇiḥ |
marunmandaṁ mandaṁ taralayati mallīmadhukarān
kimanyadvaktavyaṁ vidhurapi vidhātā samudayam || 33 ||

nikuñjaḥ ayam — this grove; guñjan-madhukara-kadamba-ākulataraḥ — thick with swarms of humming bees; prayātaḥ — has gone; prāyaḥ — probably; ayam — this; carama-giri-śṛṅgam — to the peak of the western mountain; dina-maṇiḥ — the jewel of day; marut — the breeze; mandaṁ mandam — gently, gently; taralayati — stirs; mallī-madhukarān — the bees on the jasmine; kim anyat — what else; vaktavyam — is to be said; vidhuḥ api — the moon too; vidhātā — will make; samudayam — its rising.

33this grove is thick with swarms of humming bees; the jewel of the day has probably gone behind the peak of the western mountain; the breeze gently, gently stirs the bees on the jasmine; what more is there to say — the moon too is about to rise.13

मञ्जुतरगुञ्जदलिकुञ्जमतिभीषणं
मन्दमरुदन्तरगगन्धकृतदूषणम् ॥
सकलमेतदीरितं
किं च गुरुपञ्चशरचञ्चलं मम जीवितम् ॥ ध्रु ॥
मत्तपिकदत्तरुजमुत्तमाधिकरं(?) वनं
सङ्गसुखमङ्गमपि तुङ्गभयभाजनम् ॥
रुद्रनृपमाशु विदधातु सुखसंकुलं
रामपदधामकविरायकृतमुज्ज्वलम् ॥ ३४ ॥

mañjutaraguñjadalikuñjamatibhīṣaṇaṁ
mandamarudantaragagandhakṛtadūṣaṇam ||
sakalametadīritaṁ
kiṁ ca gurupañcaśaracañcalaṁ mama jīvitam || dhru ||
mattapikadattarujamuttamādhikaraṁ(?) vanaṁ
saṅgasukhamaṅgamapi tuṅgabhayabhājanam ||
rudranṛpamāśu vidadhātu sukhasaṁkulaṁ
rāmapadadhāmakavirāyakṛtamujjvalam || 34 ||

mañjutara-guñjad-ali-kuñjam — the grove of sweetly humming bees; ati-bhīṣaṇam — is most terrible; manda-marud-antara-ga-gandha-kṛta-dūṣaṇam — the fragrance in the gentle breeze does harm; sakalam etat — all this; īritam — has been said; kiṁ ca — moreover; guru-pañca-śara-cañcalam — shaken by the heavy five arrows; mama — my; jīvitam — life; matta-pika-datta-rujam — where maddened cuckoos give pain; uttama-ādhi-karam — causing the highest torment; vanam — forest; saṅga-sukham — for the joy of union; aṅgam api — even the body; tuṅga-bhaya-bhājanam — a vessel of great fear; rudra-nṛpam — King Rudra; āśu — soon; vidadhātu — may it make; sukha-saṅkulam — full of happiness; rāma-pada-dhāma-kavi-rāya-kṛtam — made by the poet Raya, the abode of the word "Rama"; ujjvalam — radiant.

34The grove where the bees hum so sweetly is now so terrible; the gentle fragrant breeze does me harm. All this I have told you. And more: because of the heavy five arrows my life is wavering. (Refrain.) The forest, where maddened cuckoos give pain, is the highest torment; even the body, made for the joy of union, has become a vessel of great fear. May this radiant song, made by the poet Raya whose name is "Rama", soon fill King Rudra with happiness.14

Madanika. Child, look for me at the foot of the vakula tree. (Exit.)

(Exeunt the others too.)

End of the Third Act of the drama "Sri Jagannatha-vallabha", called "Bhava-prakasha".

✦

Notes

  1. Radha believes herself rejected and reproaches herself for having disregarded convention, not knowing that Krishna's refusal was only a test (Act 2). For Gaudiya Vaishnavas her readiness to sacrifice everything, even her good name, is a sign of the highest selfless love (CC Adi 4.167–169: for Krishna's sake the gopis gave up everything — worldly custom and Vedic duty alike).
  2. Sragdharā metre. The sound of Krishna's flute is called the Parabrahman in harmony with the chants of the Sama Veda: the Absolute itself is in the sound of His flute. "Beloved of Shri" (Śrīkānta) is Krishna. The end of the fourth line is corrupt in the edition and is rendered by the sense and the edition's Hindi translation. A fire of chaff (kukūla) smoulders slowly and long — an image of the unquenchable pain of separation.
  3. Shashimukhi, like Madanika, tests the firmness of Radha's love. The beginning of the verse is unclear in the edition and is rendered by the sense.
  4. Shashimukhi says that a wife stays faithful to her husband (the doe does not choose the lion) — but at once refutes herself: the lilies love the moon even when it wanes, that is, true love does not depend on the beloved's merits. A proverb spoken in consolation may mean the very opposite.
  5. Śārdūla-vikrīḍita metre. The last words of the third line are unclear in the edition and are rendered by the sense and the edition's Hindi translation.
  6. The first line is corrupt in the edition; the sense is restored from the Hindi translation: a bee once drawn to a flower does not leave it. Madanika consoles Radha: Krishna, having once seen her, will not abandon her.
  7. "Set with jewels" — that is, count every moment a treasure. The fourth line is one syllable short in the print and has been corrected by the metre.
  8. An allegory: the young tree Radha has raised is Krishna's love, nurtured by her; the bees that cling to its buds are a sign that love is about to blossom. Madanika hints at good news.
  9. Radha fears she will die of separation and asks her friend to remember her.
  10. Madanika recounts how Krishna listened to her stories about Radha: His feelings betray His love. A line of the song is partly unclear in the edition.
  11. Āryā metre. The cloud is Krishna, the water the hope of meeting, the fire the heat of separation; the doe is Radha herself. The last word is corrupt in the print and is read as bhavitā.
  12. Mandākrāntā metre. This is Krishna's verse on the picture with Radha's portrait: the lotus opening for the first time is Radha, the youth who breathes its fragrance is Krishna Himself. His earlier refusal (Act 2) was only feigned. The beginning of the fourth line is unclear in the edition.
  13. Śikhariṇī metre. Nightfall and moonrise intensify the pain of separation; Radha asks Madanika to hurry.
  14. "The poet Raya whose name is 'Rama'" is a play on the name of Ramananda Raya.
